About this species: Anabasis articulata is a jointed woody subshrub adapted to desert and semi-desert habitats. It has reduced leaves and green segmented stems that help limit water loss while maintaining photosynthesis. The plant is often associated with dry, open, and sometimes salt-affected soils, making it a good example of a xerohalophytic desert chenopod. It contributes to the structure of arid shrublands and can indicate harsh soil and moisture conditions.
Geographical distribution: SE. Spain, N. Africa to Iraq and Arabian Peninsula.
